summary.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16.6% to Rs 703 crore; FY27 guided to early-to-mid-teens growth and 27-28% margins.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 703 crore, driven by sample volume growth of 12.9%, while Q4 EBITDA rose 10.5% to Rs 187 crore at a 26.6% margin. Q4 PAT fell to Rs 132 crore from Rs 156 crore, as last year included a Rs 41 crore one-time benefit and this year had a Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge in Q3. FY26 revenue grew 12.2% to Rs 2,763 crore with a 27.2% EBITDA margin, and the Board approved a final dividend of Rs 4 per share. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to early-to-mid-teens and margins to 27-28%, while stepping up spending on labs, infrastructure and A&P.

segments.name: Swasthfit (preventive B2C brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed 27% of FY26 total revenue; management says B2C is about 75% of revenue and packages make up about 28% of revenue, including Suburban packages.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Sustained double-digit growth through the year, with added testing locations to improve turnaround time.

segments.name: West / Suburban
segments.commentary: Suburban had weak performance for about 3 quarters but showed recovery in Q4; it is now reported within West and is no longer a separate entity.

segments.name: Radiology (Sovaaka and centres)
segments.commentary: One Sovaaka premium centre launched in January 2026; no further Sovaaka centres planned in FY27. One or two radiology centres are in the FY27 capex plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at early-to-mid-teens; CEO later framed it as a 13%-15% range.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 27%-28%, similar to FY26's 27.2% including the Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 100-120 crore, covering maintenance capex plus 12-15 new labs, radiology centres and a precision lab.
Effective tax rate expected to stay around 25%.
Price increase not planned immediately; a decision is a few quarters away, depending on market response and competition.
International expansion: a Dubai/UAE subsidiary incorporated; over 3-5 years, new geographies including the Middle East are planned on top of Nepal and Bangladesh.
capex_capacity: FY26: added 14 new labs and more than 1,100 collection centres; about 32 labs and close to 2,000 collection centres added over two years.
FY27 plan: 12-15 new labs, 1-2 radiology centres and a precision diagnostic lab, on top of maintenance capex within Rs 100-120 crore.
Acquired Shahbazkers Diagnostic Centre, a single pathology-led lab in Mumbai with about Rs 6 crore revenue, for about Rs 20 crore (about 3.3x FY26 revenue); the EBITDA margin was not disclosed.
Sovaaka: one centre launched January 2026; management wants to stabilise it before any expansion.
Radiology expansion is to be slow and calibrated, with no ambitious 4-5 year targets set.
demand_pricing: FY26 patient volume growth was 5.3% (vs 4.2% in FY25); Q4 patient volume growth was 8.2%; sample volume growth was 12.9% in Q4 and 10.4% in FY26.
Tests per patient rose to 3.21 in Q4 from 3.07; revenue per patient growth was attributed to test and geographic mix.
About 39% of revenue now comes from Tier 3-plus towns; management says pricing is set by cluster, so Tier 3 growth is not dilutive.
Price increase deferred: last price rise was 3 years ago, but management is waiting because it passed on GST-related benefits.
Management said GLP-1 drugs had no differential impact on volumes.
Reagent supply: about 3-4 months of inventory and long-term contracts; a prolonged Middle East conflict could affect imported reagent supply and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other expense up sharply in Q4, and is the margin sustainable into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited infra upgrades including Delhi NCR and higher A&P spend as geographies expand; FY27 margin guided at 27-28% with investment in labs continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 19% YoY in Q4, and was there a regrouping?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 129 crore vs Rs 108 crore: courier and transport costs were regrouped from employee benefit to other expenses; the rise reflects 14 new labs and Sovaaka operations, not the Labour Code.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 tax rate near 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: A reversal of deferred tax after an income tax assessment and refund; the underlying tax rate is still about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for early-to-mid-teens FY27 growth when the post-COVID run rate was 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab and collection network additions are maturing, Delhi NCR is expected to keep growing at double digits, and Suburban is recovering; the range is 13-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is GLP-1 adding to patient volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth reflects the collection and lab network and that no differential impact from GLP-1 is being ascribed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Suburban's revenue or margin separately reported, and where does its margin stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Suburban is no longer reported separately and is part of West; management said West margins still have room to improve, and the company-wide margin is 27-28%.

risks_watch: Q4 PAT declined 15% YoY to Rs 132 crore despite revenue growth, partly due to the absence of the Rs 41 crore one-time benefit from last year.
Margin pressure from heavy investment in labs, infrastructure and A&P; FY27 margin guided at 27-28%, which is flat to FY26.
Reagent and consumable supply and cost risk from the Middle East conflict after about 3-4 months of inventory.
Patient volume growth of 8.2% in Q4 may not be sustainable; management cautioned against building it into FY27 plans.
Price increase timing is uncertain; competitive intensity and market response will determine it.
Suburban recovery and West margin improvement are not separately disclosed, which limits tracking.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and the FY27 growth outlook, but cautious on volume extrapolation and pricing, which management said will wait a few quarters. Management was less specific on Suburban and radiology economics and did not disclose the Shahbazkers margin.
key_quotes: We are entering FY27 with strong operational momentum, a strengthened digital infrastructure, and a clear pathway towards sustaining early to mid -teens revenue growth.
So the 8.2% patient volume growth that we have seen in this quarter is something which I would not hastily built into the plan for next year.

The cluster pricing remains the same and parallelly, even when I am going into the Tier 3, Tier 4 towns, with more access, we will be able to sell our health packages, preventive check-ups and all of those, which even on a revenue side per patient side is slightly higher revenue.
